newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower after sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower after sluggish trade.

text.p: Philippine shares closed in negative territory on Monday amid low volume as profit-taking in several firstliner issues outweighed early gains attributed to PLDT's climb in New York, traders said.
"We actually have a dearth of stories to tell. Nobody is talking of surprises so the tendency of the market is to stay where it is," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities Phils Inc.
Turnover was a mere 1.05 billion pesos. The main index closed 10.75 points lower at 2,790.86.
"We are seeing some retracement in issues which rose recently. As long as volumes are not too heavy on the sell side then we are alright," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
PLDT's ADR, which climbed $1 3/8 to $60 7/8 in New York, pushed up the issue in the domestic market by closing five pesos higher at 830 pesos.
But in the broad market, losers slightly outnumbered gainers 58 to 56 with 72 issues unchanged. All the sub-indices fell, except for the financial and banking index.

"There appears to be no fresh incentive to get players back into the market so the large majority are and will be on the sidelines," said Louie Bate, managing director for equities brokerage at ING Baring Securities.
Orion-Squire Capital research head Cilette Liboro said the market may test the 2,750 level in the next few days before moving further.
